6 tips for hiring translators for your international B2B deals

February 19, 2018
Business Tips | Good to Know | Translation services

Selling to other businesses abroad means your content has to work in front of procurement teams, engineers, finance directors and lawyers. B2B translation covers far more than a brochure, and the quality of your translations shapes how seriously overseas buyers take you.

Before you brief a provider, work through these six checks. They will save you time, cost and awkward corrections later.

Define your target market and buyer

Start with who you are talking to. A technical buyer in Germany reads differently from a purchasing manager in Spain, and both differ from a UK reader.

Tell your translator who the audience is, what you want them to do and what tone suits your brand. A translator who knows the reader can make a proposal sound confident without being pushy.

Confirm the language pair and the regional variety

Once you know your markets, list every language and variety you need. Many languages differ from country to country, so one version rarely covers every market.

French is a good example. The French used in France, Canada, Belgium and Switzerland differs in vocabulary, formal conventions and sometimes in legal terms. Our French translators can advise whether one version will serve several countries or whether you need separate ones.

Browse the languages we cover to see where you can expand.

Choose a translator who knows your sector

Linguistic skill is the starting point. Your translator also needs to understand your industry, because B2B content is full of specialist terms that must be used consistently.

A medical equipment manufacturer needs a translator with medical experience for its instructions. A software company needs someone who knows the vocabulary of IT, and a law firm needs a legal translator. Check our industry specialisms and ask any provider for examples in your field.

Plan for localisation, not just translation

Translation replaces words. Localisation adapts the whole message to the market, including formats, units, currencies, examples, humour and cultural references.

For B2B localisation services, ask your provider how they handle dates, currencies, measurements, legal references and calls to action. A phrase that persuades a UK buyer can sound abrupt or overfamiliar in another business culture.

Our document translation and localisation teams work with you to adapt the message and keep terminology consistent across brochures, proposals and tender documents.

Translate your website for each buyer market

Overseas buyers will check your website before they reply to an email. If it is only in English, you ask them to work harder, and some will turn to automated translation that can mangle technical detail.

B2B website translation tells those buyers you are serious about their market. It covers product pages, case studies, terms and conditions, forms and metadata, so search engines in that country can find you too. Read about our website translation service for the steps involved.

Check local rules and documents

Countries differ in what a business document must contain. Labelling, safety information, instructions, disclaimers and contract terms can be subject to local requirements, and errors can cause costly delays.

Research the rules for each market, and ask your translation service how it handles legal and regulatory content. Contracts should be translated by a specialist, and you should keep the original and the translation together. Take legal advice from a qualified adviser in the country concerned, because a translator cannot replace it.

What to ask before you hire

A short list of questions makes comparing providers much easier:

  • Who translates the text, and are they native speakers of the target language?
  • Does a second linguist review every translation?
  • Can the provider use your glossary and style guide, and build one for you?
  • How does the provider protect confidential documents?
  • Which formats can it return, and how does it handle updates to existing content?

Our professional translators work into their mother tongue, and every project is reviewed before delivery. If you are planning to take your business overseas, request a free, no-obligation quote and tell us your markets and sectors.

Frequently asked questions

What is B2B translation?

B2B translation is the translation of content that businesses use to sell to and work with other businesses. It includes proposals, contracts, catalogues, websites, manuals and marketing material. It needs sector knowledge as well as language skill.

How do I choose a B2B translation provider?

Look for native translators with experience in your sector, a clear review process and a way to manage terminology. Ask for examples of similar projects. A short sample translation can help you compare.

What is the difference between translation and localisation for B2B?

Translation converts the text into another language. Localisation also adapts formats, currencies, examples and tone to the target market. For B2B, it helps your content sound natural to local buyers.

Do I need to translate my website for B2B buyers?

If you want serious enquiries from overseas, yes. Buyers are more likely to trust and contact a supplier that speaks their language. A translated website also gives search engines in that market something to index.

Should I use machine translation for B2B documents?

Machine translation can help with internal drafts, but it can make mistakes with technical terms and nuance. For contracts, regulated content and anything customer-facing, use a professional translator to check the final text.
